title: Normalized finite reductions of the exceptional unit trace
statement: Fix D,C,E,f,d,S as in def-pur-unit-trace-scalar-data, a counit-normalized finite right realization normal, a completed unit pullback core and finite-Tor membership hT for the shifted Tate unit T. Let g:T≅S.G(1_Y) be any isomorphism such that sourceUnitIso.hom followed by g.hom has the prescribed finite smooth-purity reductions. Then the actual unitTrace(S,core,hT,g), obtained by compact support of g followed by the specified exceptional counit, satisfies HasTraceReductions at every positive exponent. No existence or uniqueness of such a g is claimed.

proof.text:
For $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z$ let $b_r:(P_0M)_r\xrightarrow{\sim}P_AM_r$ and $v_r:(G_0N)_r\xrightarrow{\sim}G_AN_r$ be the canonical integral reduction comparisons. Compact-support reduction and the integral exceptional-adjoint theorem give these maps and the counit identity $\epsilon_{A,N_r}P_A(v_r)=(\epsilon_{0,N})_r b_r^{-1}$. Naturality of $b_r$ therefore gives, for $t_0=\epsilon_{0,\mathbf1}P_0(g_0)$,
$$(t_0)_r b_{r,T_0}^{-1}=\epsilon_{A,\mathbf1}P_A\bigl(v_r(g_0)_r\bigr)=\epsilon_{A,\mathbf1}P_A(\gamma_{f,A_Y}).$$
The last equality uses exactly the prescribed reduction of $g_0$; the right side is the normalized finite smooth trace by its definition. This calculation works for any of the permitted choices of $g_0$.

proof.text: In the preceding counit calculation expand HasPrescribedReductions and HasTraceReductions. Naturality of reduction and support allows cancelling reduction of sourceUnitIso.hom against its inverse. The remaining composite is coefficientValuedSmoothTrace by its definition, giving exactly the heterogeneous equality of HasTraceReductions. The calculation is valid at every positive exponent for any permitted g.
